property_summary: For any inputs to initialize, the deployed contract's public baseToken equals the _baseToken argument passed to initialize; the mutant that force-sets baseToken to address(0) will violate this for any non-zero _baseToken.

For any inputs to initialize, the deployed pool's baseToken equals the provided _baseToken (reference); the mutant erroneously sets baseToken to the factory address, so there exist inputs for which c.baseToken() != _baseToken.

For any inputs to initialize, the contract's public baseToken getter returns the _baseToken argument passed to initialize; the mutant wrongly sets baseToken to the nft argument for some inputs, breaking this invariant.

After initialize(...) completes, the contract's nft() getter returns the same address that was passed as the _nft argument; the mutant breaks this by setting nft to address(0) instead of the provided value for some inputs.

For any inputs to initialize(...), the correct contract sets c.nft() equal to the _nft argument passed to initialize; the mutant instead sets nft to the factory-derived owner address for some inputs, so there exist inputs where c.nft() != _nft.

For every call to initialize(...) the contract's public nft() equals the _nft argument passed in (reference satisfies this for all inputs); the mutant sets nft to a different address (the factory owner) for some inputs, so there exist inputs where c.nft() != _nft.

For every call to initialize(...), the reference contract stores the exact _nft argument in c.nft(); the mutant sometimes stores a different address (the factory.ownerOf(...) result) so there exist inputs where c.nft() != the _nft argument.

For every call to initialize(...), the reference contract sets c.nft() to the _nft argument passed; the mutant instead may set c.nft() to an address derived from the factory (Factory(factory).ownerOf(...)) for some inputs, so there exist init arguments where c.nft() != the provided _nft.

For every call to initialize(...), the reference contract stores in c.nft() an address whose ownerOf on the factory (when interpreted as an ERC721 token id equal to the pool address cast to uint160) is irrelevant — concretely the reference always sets c.nft() equal to the _nft argument passed to initialize, while the mutant sets c.nft() to Factory(factory).ownerOf(uint160(address(this))) for some inputs, so there exist fuzzed _nft values where after initialize the stored nft != the provided _nft.

For any inputs to initialize, the contract's nft getter returns the nft address argument passed to initialize (i.e. c.nft() == _nft); the mutant that assigns nft = msg.sender breaks this by making c.nft() != _nft for some inputs.

After any initialize(...) call that succeeds, the contract's public changeFee equals the _changeFee parameter passed to initialize (reference); the mutant increments and thus will make changeFee != _changeFee for some inputs.

For any inputs to initialize, the contract's public changeFee equals the _changeFee argument passed (the reference sets changeFee = _changeFee); the mutant that forces changeFee to 0 will violate this when _changeFee != 0.

For any inputs to initialize, the contract's stored changeFee equals the _changeFee argument passed (i.e., changeFee == _changeFee); the mutant doubles the stored value so it violates this property for inputs where _changeFee != 0.

For any callers and any _feeRate input within allowed bounds, calling initialize(...) sets the contract's public feeRate to the provided _feeRate; the mutant sets feeRate to 0 instead, so there exist inputs where c.feeRate() != _feeRate after initialize.

For any inputs to initialize, the deployed contract's public feeRate equals the _feeRate argument given to initialize; the mutant assigns feeRate from _changeFee instead and thus can make feeRate != _feeRate for some inputs.

For every valid initialize(...) call the reference contract sets feeRate equal to the _feeRate argument (i.e. feeRate() == _feeRate after initialize), whereas the mutant defers setting feeRate until after initialized which can cause feeRate to remain zero during initialization-observable calls and thus break this property for some inputs.

For any inputs to initialize, after initialize returns the public getter feeRate() equals the provided _feeRate; the mutant that delays setting feeRate can cause intermediate calls during initialize (triggered via a reentrant receiver on safeTransferFrom when transferring an ERC721 into the contract during initialization) to observe feeRate() == 0, breaking the rule for some inputs.

For every call to initialize(...) the contract's public feeRate() getter equals the _feeRate argument after initialization completes; the mutant that moves setting feeRate until after initialized allows a reentrant ERC721 receiver called during initialization to observe feeRate() == 0 (breaking the rule for some inputs).
